claim: Without a surrogate, the formatted type T always goes through contractless mode. Any [MessagePackObject]/[Key]/[IgnoreMember] or [DataContract]/[DataMember] attributes on T are ignored. The acceptance criterion says 'If T does carry MessagePack attributes, they are honoured' (the maintainer said 'If there are attributes on it, fine, we'll use them'). The change instead serializes every public read-write member under its name as a string key. As a result, members marked [IgnoreMember], or left out of a [DataContract], are still serialized, and [Key(int)] ordinals are replaced by name keys.

claim: Without a surrogate, the collector always uses contractless mode and never reads attributes on T. `[DataContract]`/`[DataMember(Name)]`, `[IgnoreDataMember]`, `[MessagePackObject]`/`[Key]` and `[IgnoreMember]` are all ignored. The acceptance criteria require T's attributes to be honoured. Concrete input: a referenced type `[DataContract] class MyObject { [DataMember(Name="a")] public int Included {get;set;} public int NotAMember {get;set;} }`. On head the generated formatter serializes `NotAMember` under the key "NotAMember" and `Included` under "Included" instead of "a". That breaks wire compatibility with the dynamic resolver, and members the author excluded are serialized anyway.

claim: IsPartial checks only the formatter's own declaration. Consider a formatter nested in a non-partial containing type, for example `public class Outer { [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] internal partial class F : IMessagePackFormatter<T> {} }`. It passes the check, and the template then emits the nesting `partial class Outer { partial class F ... }`. The result is CS0260 (missing partial modifier on Outer) instead of a MsgPack019 diagnostic.

claim: Constructor-less handling: for structs and for classes the collector passes empty constructorParameters and always treats every member as writable/settable. Members that are init-only or required are marked IsWritable: true with IsInitOnly set. If the generator emits object-initializer or direct assignment for properties whose setter is public but init-only it is fine, but required members on contractless types are not enforced, so deserialization can silently leave required members unset. This is a correctness edge, not a security hole.

claim: GetInstanceMembers keeps only the most-derived member of each name. Take a derived class that overrides only the getter (`public override int X { get => ...; }`) of a base read-write property. The member is silently dropped from the contractless contract, although the property is writable through the base setter.
